top_signal.title: Is 10k reasonable for an accountant fees? And also is it normal for accountants to not give give retirement contribution advice ?
top_signal.summary: My husband and I are looking for a new accountant. We’re both self employed, seperate endeavors, he owns a business with employees, I’m a business of one.   We were quoted 10k from an accountant we were recommended at a reputable firm to handle his s-corp, my schedule c, personal returns, and returns for another business my husband owns. Is this typical? My income is not complicated (I get a few big payouts every year) but I understand my husband’s is more so, and that the new accountant would have to step in and finish the s-corp setup that our old one failed to do. If this is what it costs that’s fine, we were just a bit surprised.   Something I didn’t love is when we asked if I should close my SEP-IRA to roll into a solo 401k to maximize contributions, he hemmed and hawed and said we would need to talk to someone on their wealth management team who would take over the funds. We’re not opposed to working with a financial advisor, but I don’t love the idea that we  have  to just to know how much we should be putting away…I was planning to max my contribution this year regardless, but found it odd.   We’re in Michigan, if that matters.       submitted by     /u/eggbride       [link]       [comments]
